placement.position_note: PLACED 2026-08-09. The corner is documented — chicagology and the Chicago Landmark record both put the Sauganash at the south-east corner of Lake and Market — but the COORDINATE is inferred, so the tag follows the weaker half. Method: Market Street is today's N Wacker Drive and Lake Street is unchanged, an equivalence the research dossier states and the georeference independently corroborates, since the 1834 plats warped onto the modern street centrelines at 17.5 m RMS. The modern intersection centre was read from OpenStreetMap (EPSG:26916 E 447161.9, N 4637285.4) and the footprint origin offset 12.2 m east and 20.2 m south of it: half of an 80 ft platted street to reach the kerb, and the footprint's own 8 m depth so the building's north face sits on the Lake Street frontage of a south-east corner lot. Working uncertainty about 20 m, which is the georeference's, not an additional guess. Facade bearing 0 (north, onto Lake Street): the sources say it faced the forks to the north-west, so the true bearing is likely nearer 315, but the plat lot lines are orthogonal and a corner building fronting Lake is the defensible reading until better evidence appears.
placement.symbolic_location: South-east corner of Lake Street and Market Street (today Lake St and N Wacker Dr).

footprint.note: THE TWO-MASS PLAN, AND THE 12 x 8 m PLACEHOLDER IS RETIRED (T-0626, spending T-0617's reading). THE FRONTAGE IS DERIVED AND THE DEPTH IS NOT, and the block is graded at the weaker of the two. FRONTAGE 9.92 m: Braunhold's engraving draws five bays on the street face and rectified against that face's own vanishing point the five are EQUAL to 2.4 % (tools/measure_sauganash_plate.py, bay_rhythm.rectified_gaps 0.997 / 1.011 / 1.020 / 0.972). The bay measures 1.984 m at the plate's stated scale datum — a standing adult at 1.70 m, hat included, the two men on the walk reading 147 and 143 px — so five bays are 9.92 m. THE DATUM'S BIAS IS SMALL AND BOUNDED, which is what makes this a measurement rather than a floor: the men stand a pace forward of the wall, and the plate's own focal length puts them 43.0 m from the station (f 3664.7 px on a 145 px figure of 1.70 m), so a pace is 2.7 %. The frontage is therefore 9.9-10.2 m and 12 m IS REFUTED rather than merely unsupported. The value taken is the measured 9.92 and is not fudged up into the correction. What does still move it is the 1.70 m datum itself: at 1.60 m the frontage reads 9.3 m and at 1.80 m 10.5 m. DEPTH 8.0 m IS UNCHANGED AND IS STILL A RECONSTRUCTION. One plate gives no depth (docs/RESEARCH/sauganash_image_accuracy.md row 11), so nothing has measured it; it is held at the placeholder's own figure deliberately, because the placement above offsets this origin by the footprint's own 8 m depth to stand the north face on the Lake Street frontage, and moving a number with no evidence behind it would move the building. THE SECOND MASS IS NOT IN THIS POLYGON, on the precedent green_tree_tavern's rear ell set: an attached wing is the archetype's, sized by this phase's own form attributes (cross_wing, cross_wing_depth_m, cross_wing_end), and the polygon is the main block's plan. The one lead this note used to carry is still open: Andreas vol. 1 p. 106 ('Eagle Exchange'), not yet read at page-image level, and the individual building rectangle on Hathaway 1834. NOTE ON WHAT THIS TAG MEANS: conjectural here is about SIZE, not about existence or character. That the building was a two-storey white frame block is documented (Wau-Bun); how big it was is measured off one retrospective sheet and no better. The renderer therefore does NOT dither the massing on account of this tag — see generators/archetypes/frame_tavern.py — and the dimensional uncertainty is carried in the sidecar instead.

liberty.title: Sauganash roof join and stack section
liberty.text:
Sauganash roof join and stack section
DECISION
The Sauganash Hotel's roof junction and stack section are reconstructed trials, not measurements from Andreas/Braunhold's retrospective 1884 engraving. The existing wing helper gives its roof the main ridge height but stops its crest 3.75 m short of the main ridge. An explicit Hotel-only shared-ridge option now ends that crest at the main roof's centre, using the existing depth and roof overhang. The existing site, footprint, wall heights, pitch and unmeasured outer wing depth stay selected as before. The intended join is not proof of an exact historical junction or a July-1835 alteration date. The two ridge-end brick stacks retain their stations, plain heads and ridge + 0.55 m tops. Their square section is tried at 0.60 m instead of the inherited 0.90 m, to address the visibly broad shaft profile. The 0.60 m is reconstructed, not metres read from the plate or from a source-calibrated camera. No cap lip, new height, date, historical camera, occupant or material is asserted. These working choices leave other buildings as they were. They remain subject to comparison with the pictures and ordinary street views, and do not themselves establish an image match.
SOURCES
"THE SAUGANASH HOTEL." — wood engraving, in A. T. Andreas, History of Chicago…, a verified public-domain retrospective plate, used for relative form.
